classification.difficultyReason: Find both dimensional upper bounds, then use them to calculate an area upper bound.

content.prompt: Determine the upper limit for the area of this rectangle.

spec.description: Unshaded horizontal rectangle, with 14 cm below the bottom edge and 6 cm beside the right edge. Ordinary outline and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: Rectangle with measured length 14 cm and width 6 cm; stated measurements imply precision 1 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions are visible; upper bounds and area are answer content.

answer.worked:
The precision is $1\,\mathrm{cm}$, so the absolute error is $\tfrac12\times1=0.5\,\mathrm{cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Upper length}&=14+0.5=14.5\,\mathrm{cm}\\
\text{Upper width}&=6+0.5=6.5\,\mathrm{cm}\\
\text{Upper area}&=14.5\times6.5\\
&=94.25\,\mathrm{cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
